samples.summary: Non-OK response body is never drained/cancelled before throwing, leaking the socket
samples.evidence: In the fetch loop, `if (!location) { if (!res.ok) { throw new Error(`Image fetch failed: ${res.status} ...`) } ... }` (lines 578-583) throws while `res.body` is still unread. The same function deliberately cancels the redirect body two lines later (`await res.body?.cancel().catch(() => {})`, line 589) precisely because "an unread one holds its socket open". On a document full of failing images (a realistic case now that failures are tolerated via `onImageError`) every 4xx/5xx hop leaves an undrained undici body, holding connections until GC/keep-alive timeout. The same gap exists for the `res.status === 0` throw (line 567).

samples.summary: Declared-Content-Length rejection throws without cancelling the body stream
samples.evidence: `const declared = Number(res.headers.get('content-length')); if (Number.isFinite(declared) && declared > maxBytes) throw tooLarge();` throws before the reader is obtained, so `res.body` is left un-cancelled — unlike the streaming overflow path a few lines below which does `await reader.cancel().catch(() => {})` (line 641). Inconsistent resource handling on the exact path most likely to hit a large in-flight response.

samples.summary: `isAllowedHost` compares `url.host`, so an operator entry that spells the scheme-default port never matches
samples.evidence: `const host = url.host.toLowerCase()...; return allowedHosts.some(h => h === host || h === hostname);` — `URL.host` omits the port when it is the scheme default, so `WAFFLEBASE_IMAGE_HOSTS=minio.internal:443` will not match `https://minio.internal/blob.png` and `h:80` will not match `http://h/x`, even though those are exactly the same endpoint. `sameHostAsServer` right above uses `effectivePort()` to normalise this; `isAllowedHost` does not, so the documented `host:port` form silently fails for default ports and the operator's opt-in is ignored (export drops the image).

samples.summary: Missing media entry now silently drops the image element instead of raising the previous explicit error
samples.evidence: `resolveImageRId` used to `throw new Error('exportPptx: image src not found in media map: ...')` for a src absent from `srcToMediaPath`; it now unconditionally `return null`, and `group.ts:66` turns that into `''`. The comment asserts the only way to reach it is a caller-tolerated fetch failure, but the branch is not conditioned on `opts.onImageError` — any future pre-scan gap (an image reachable through a container `flattenElements` does not walk, a src mutated between pre-scan and serialization) now produces a deck missing content with no error and no reporter call, for browser callers too. Gating the `null` return on `opts.onImageError` being set would keep the loud failure for the unintended case.

samples.summary: `dialOnce` can throw `undefined` if handed an empty dial list
samples.evidence: `let lastError: unknown; for (const dial of dials) {...} throw lastError;` — with `dials.length === 0` this throws `undefined`, which `outputError`/`reportSkippedImage` would render as the string "undefined". Today `pinnedUrls` always returns at least one entry so it is unreachable, but the defensive path is wrong; a `throw lastError ?? new Error(...)` costs nothing.

samples.summary: A failed image src is re-fetched and re-reported once per DOCX part
samples.evidence: `collectImages` is invoked with a separate `entries` array for body, header and footer (lines 104/119/131), and the failure record `entries.push({ rId: '', path: '', ext: '', src })` only dedupes within one part. An image used in both the body and the header therefore triggers two fetch attempts and two `onImageError` (stderr) lines for the same URL.

finding.summary: `slides export` (PPTX) has no per-image tolerance, so the new SSRF guard turns a previously-working image into a total export failure
finding.evidence: The change deliberately makes a refused/unreachable image an ordinary outcome and patches both docs paths for it (`pdf-image-painter.ts:99-101` catches and reports; `docx-exporter.ts:448-455` records a failed entry). The slides path was not patched: `packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:209` builds the same guarded `createImageFetcher`, `packages/cli/src/slides/pptx-export.ts:14` awaits it unguarded, and `exportPptx` calls `await opts.fetchImage(src)` at `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/index.ts:162` with no try/catch. Any deck whose image `src` names a non-public host that is not the configured server (an internal MinIO/blob host that used to be fetched fine, a stale intranet URL, or a name whose DNS lookup fails) now rejects and the whole `slides export deck.pptx` aborts through `outputError`, where before this change the image was fetched and embedded.

finding.summary: Address-pinning plain-`http:` image fetches sends `Host: <ip>` on Node, breaking name-based virtual hosts that worked before
finding.evidence: `pinnedUrls` (line 396-404) rewrites every `http:` target's hostname to a resolved IP, and `dialOnce` tries to compensate with `headers: { host }` (line 491). The code's own comment at 476-480 states Node's undici drops `host` as a forbidden header name, so the request really arrives as `Host: <ip>`. Any public image served over plain http from a shared/vhosted origin (very common for CDNs and reverse proxies) will now get the wrong site or a 404 instead of the image. Combined with the new silent-drop behaviour in the docx/pdf exporters, the image just disappears from the export with only a `console.warn`. This is a behaviour regression on a path that worked before the change.
